//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// CallOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_CallOp : MGP_Op<"call", [
  CallOpInterface,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<SymbolUserOpInterface>,
]> {
  let summary = "Call a subgraph.";
  let description = [{
    Placeholder for the execute block of the !mgp.model named by `callee`,
    replaced by mef.callables and grt.invoke ops by
    `ConvertSubgraphsToCallablesPass`.

    Operands and results must match the signature of the target model's execute block.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    mgp.model @subgraph : mof {
      init (...) {
        // ...
      }
      execute (%ch: !mef.chain, %ctx: !mgp.context, %weights: !mgp.opaque, %cpu: mgp.opaque, %arg: tensor<?x4x16xf32>)
              -> (!mef.chain, tensor<?x10xf32>) {
        // ...
      }
    }

    mgp.model @main : mof {
      init (...) {
        // ...
      }
      execute (%ch: !mef.chain, %ctx: !mgp.context, %weights: !mgp.opaque, %cpu: mgp.opaque, %arg: tensor<?x4x16xf32>)
              -> (!mef.chain, tensor<?x10xf32>) {
        %sub_res = mgp.call @subgraph(%ch, %ctx, %weights, %cpu, %arg)
      }
    }
    ```
  }];
  let arguments = (ins
    FlatSymbolRefAttr:$callee,
    DefaultValuedAttr<StrAttr, "\"\"">:$prefix,
    Variadic<AnyType>:$operands,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$isGlobalizedIndex,

    // Needed to satisfy CallOpInterface
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<DictArrayAttr, "{}">:$arg_attrs,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<DictArrayAttr, "{}">:$res_attrs
  );
  let results = (outs Variadic<AnyType>:$results);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $callee `(` $operands `)`
    (`arg_attrs` `=` $arg_attrs^)?
    (`isGlobalizedIndex` `=` $isGlobalizedIndex^)?
    (`prefix` `=` $prefix^)?
    (`res_attrs` `=` $res_attrs^)?
    attr-dict `:` functional-type($operands, results)
  }];

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    /// Get the argument operands to the called function.
    operand_range getArgOperands() {
      return getOperands();
    }

    MutableOperandRange getArgOperandsMutable() {
      return getOperandsMutable();
    }

    operand_iterator arg_operand_begin() { return operand_begin(); }
    operand_iterator arg_operand_end() { return operand_end(); }

    FlatSymbolRefAttr getCalleeSymbol() {
      return cast<FlatSymbolRefAttr>(getCalleeAttr());
    }

    /// Return the callee of this operation.
    CallInterfaceCallable getCallableForCallee() {
      return getCalleeAttr();
    }

    /// Set the callee for this operation.
    void setCalleeFromCallable(CallInterfaceCallable callee) {
      this->setCalleeAttr(cast<FlatSymbolRefAttr>(cast<SymbolRefAttr>(callee)));
    }
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// StringCreateOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def StringCreateOp : MGP_Op<"string.create", [Pure]> {
  let summary = "Creates a Mojo String from a string attribute.";
  let description = [{
    Returns an opaque pointer to a Mojo `String`, created from a Mojo
    `Pointer[String]`.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    %str = mgp.string.create "abcd" : !mgp.opaque<"mojo_string">
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins StrAttr:$value);
  let results = (outs MGP_OpaqueType:$result);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $value attr-dict `:` qualified(type($result))
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// StringConcatOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def StringConcatOp : MGP_Op<"string.concat", [Pure]> {
  let summary = "Concatenates two Mojo Strings.";
  let description = [{
    Returns a new Mojo String. Both inputs must be opaque pointers to Mojo
    `String` values (as created by `mgp.string.create`).

    Example:
    ```mlir
    %prefix = mgp.string.create "hello " : !mgp.opaque<"mojo_string">
    %end = mgp.string.create "world" : !mgp.opaque<"mojo_string">
    %result = mgp.string.concat %prefix, %end : (!mgp.opaque<"mojo_string">, !mgp.opaque<"mojo_string">) -> !mgp.opaque<"mojo_string">
    // %result contains "hello world"
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins MGP_OpaqueType:$prefix, MGP_OpaqueType:$end);
  let results = (outs MGP_OpaqueType:$result);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $prefix `,` $end attr-dict `:` functional-type(operands, results)
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
//
// Device-generic operations in the MGP dialect. Most accept (at least one)
// #M.device_ref attribute giving the device type and 'virtual' id. Ops that
// also reference the 'host' device implement `MGP_HasDeviceOpInterface`.
//
// `DevicePrimitivesPass` renames ops implementing `MGP_HasDeviceOpInterface`
// with their device's label as a suffix and replaces #M.device_ref attributes
// with the device id. This keeps first-class device attributes for lowering
// and MGP-level transformations while dispatching directly to per-device
// primitives without handling labels at runtime.
//
// Chains in MGP are plain `!mef.chain` values.
//
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

class MGP_DeviceOp<string mnemonic, list<Trait> traits = []> :
  MGP_Op<mnemonic, [
    DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_HasDeviceOpInterface>,
  ] # traits>;

def MGP_OptDeviceRefAttr :
  DefaultValuedAttr<M_DeviceRefAttr, "kCPULabel, 0">;

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceContextProfileStartOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def DeviceContextProfileStartOp : MGP_DeviceOp<"device.context.profile.start"> {
  let summary = "Shim to tag the start of a device context profiling run";
  let description = [{Temporary op for onnx profiling; should use max-driver instead.}];

  // CAUTION: The attribute arguments must be in alphabetical order by their
  // names.
  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$deviceContext,
    MGP_OptDeviceRefAttr:$bDevice,  // 1
    StrAttr:$cTag,
    StrAttr:$dFilePath  // 2
  );
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $inChain `,` $deviceContext `,` ( `device` $bDevice^ )?
      `cTag` `=` $cTag `,` `dFilePath` `=` $dFilePath
      attr-dict `:` qualified(type($deviceContext))
  }];
  let hasVerifier = 1;
  let extraClassDefinition = [{

    M::DeviceRefAttr DeviceContextProfileStartOp::getDevice() { return getBDevice(); }
  }];
}

def DeviceContextProfileEndOp : MGP_DeviceOp<"device.context.profile.end"> {
  let summary = "Shim to tag the end of a device context profiling run";
  let description = [{Temporary op for onnx profiling; should use max-driver instead.}];

  // CAUTION: The attribute arguments must be in alphabetical order by their
  // names.
  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$deviceContext,
    MGP_OptDeviceRefAttr:$bDevice,  // 1
    StrAttr:$cTag,
    StrAttr:$dFilePath  // 2
  );
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $inChain `,` $deviceContext `,` ( `device` $bDevice^ )?
      `cTag` `=` $cTag `,` `dFilePath` `=` $dFilePath
      attr-dict `:` qualified(type($deviceContext))
  }];
  let hasVerifier = 1;
  let extraClassDefinition = [{

    M::DeviceRefAttr DeviceContextProfileEndOp::getDevice() { return getBDevice(); }
  }];
}


//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// ModuleLoadOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def ModuleLoadOp : MGP_DeviceOp<"module.load", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_HasRuntimeSlotOpInterface>,
]> {
  let summary = "Loads functions and constants for device from compiled module.";
  let description = [{
    Loads functions and constants from a compiled module encoded into a byte
    array (or, for unit testing only, a multi-line string), associated with the
    runtime in the given `!mgp.context` slot. The module gets the device's next
    module index, and each function and constant the next index within it (all
    starting at 0). Functions are referenced by (module index, function index)
    in `mgp.generic.execute`, constants by (module index, constant index) in
    `mgp.buffer.constant.load`.

    Each device type may use its own module representation in the host runtime.

    Note that this operation accepts and returns `!mef.chain`s since it is
    part of device setup on the host.

    Example:
    ```mlir
      %ch0 : !mef.chain
      %ctx : !mgp.context
      // Load a CUDA PTX or cubin module with given exported kernel and
      // constant names. The CUDA module will be associated with the CUDA
      // runtime established in slot 5, which should be for the CUDA GPU with
      // virtual device id 3.
      %ch1 = mgp.module.load %ch0, %ctx[5][1],
               dense_resource<label> : !M.aligned_bytes<1000, align 16>,
               ["kernel1", "kernel2"], ["const1", "const2"]
               device <"gpu", 3>
      %ch1 : !mef.chain
    ```
  }];

  // CAUTION: The attribute arguments must be in alphabetical order by their
  // names.
  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_ContextType:$theContext,
    UI64Attr:$aRuntimeSlot,  // 0
    AnyAttrOf<[M_MultiLineStringAttr, ElementsAttr]>:$bImage,  // 1
    M_MultiLineStringAttr:$cFunctionSymbols,  // 2
    M_MultiLineStringAttr:$dConstantSymbols,  // 3
    MGP_OptDeviceRefAttr:$eDevice,  // 4
    UI64Attr:$fModuleIndex,  // 5
    DefaultValuedAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$gDebuginfo  // 6
  );
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $inChain `,` $theContext `[` $aRuntimeSlot `]` `[` $fModuleIndex `]` `,` $bImage `,`
    $cFunctionSymbols `,` $dConstantSymbols
    ( `device` $eDevice^ )? ( `debuginfo` $gDebuginfo^ )? attr-dict
  }];
  let hasVerifier = 1;

  let extraClassDefinition = [{
    uint64_t ModuleLoadOp::getSlot() { return getARuntimeSlot(); }

    M::DeviceRefAttr ModuleLoadOp::getDevice() { return getEDevice(); }
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// ModuleLoadPlaceholder
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def ModuleLoadPlaceholderOp : MGP_Op<"module.load.placeholder"> {
  let summary = "Placeholder for the module load";
  let description = [{
    Provides a chain linking the compiled execute to the module load op in
    init. Added just before lowering the kernel ABI, and removed once the load
    module op is created.
  }];
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferConstantExternalOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def BufferConstantExternalOp : MGP_DeviceOp<"buffer.constant.external", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_LiftableBufferCreateOpInterface, ["isTrivial"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_SelectiveLowerAttrOpInterface, [
    "getLiftableAttributes",
    "getIgnorableAttributes"
  ]>,
  InferTypeOpAdaptor,
]> {
  let summary = "Initializes a buffer from an external constant.";
  let description = [{
    Returns an `!mgp.buffer` on the given device, backed at runtime by the
    pointer a weights registry (a map from names to pointers) holds for `name`.
    The name is an `!mgp.opaque<"mojo_string">`, typically from
    `mgp.string.create` (and optionally `mgp.string.concat` for prefixes).
    The pointer must respect the op's alignment. Like mgp.buffer.constant, the
    buffer's lifetime is untracked and assumed to outlive graph execution.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    %weights : !mgp.opaque<"weights_registry">
    %ch : !mef.chain
    %name = mgp.string.create "foo" : !mgp.opaque<"mojo_string">
    // Return a buffer corresponding to the named weight "foo" in the
    // weights registry.
    %buf = mgp.buffer.constant.external %ch, %weights[%name, 16384, align 16]
      : !mgp.opaque<"weights_registry">, !mgp.opaque<"mojo_string"> -> !mgp.buffer
    ```
  }];

  // CAUTION: The attribute arguments must be in alphabetical order by their
  // names.
  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_OpaqueType:$weightsRegistry,
    MGP_OpaqueType:$name,
    UI64Attr:$aSize,  // 0
    UI64Attr:$bAlign,  // 1
    MGP_OptDeviceRefAttr:$cDevice,  // 2
    DefaultValuedAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$dHasAlias,  // 3
    DefaultValuedAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$eIsPlaceholder  // 4
  );

  let results = (outs MGP_DeviceBufferType:$outBuffer);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $inChain `,` $weightsRegistry
    `[`
    $name `,` $aSize `,` `align` $bAlign
    oilist( `has_alias` $dHasAlias
          | `placeholder` $eIsPlaceholder
          | `device` $cDevice)
    `]`
    attr-dict `:` qualified(type($weightsRegistry)) `,` qualified(type($name))
    `->` qualified(type($outBuffer))
  }];
  let hasVerifier = 1;

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    /// Returns the buffer's alignment.
    std::optional<uint64_t> getOptAlign();
  }];

  let extraClassDefinition = [{
    SmallVector<Attribute> BufferConstantExternalOp::getLiftableAttributes() {
      return {getASizeAttr(), getBAlignAttr()};
    }

    SmallVector<Attribute> BufferConstantExternalOp::getIgnorableAttributes() {
      return {getCDeviceAttr(), getDHasAliasAttr()};
    }

    M::DeviceRefAttr BufferConstantExternalOp::getDevice() { return getCDevice(); }

    bool BufferConstantExternalOp::isTrivial() { return false; }
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferAllocOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def BufferAllocOp : MGP_DeviceOp<"buffer.alloc", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_BufferAllocOpInterface, ["getOutBuffer"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_LiftableBufferCreateOpInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_SelectiveLowerAttrOpInterface, ["getIgnorableAttributes"]>,
  InferTypeOpAdaptor,
]> {
  let summary = "Allocates a buffer with dynamically provided byte size on "
                "given device.";
  let description = [{
    Allocates (possibly asynchronously) an uninitialized buffer from a device's
    default memory pool with given byte size, and optional statically known
    alignment. The allocation uses the device-appropriate runtime established
    in the given `!mgp.context` slot. Not all devices support the notion of
    alignment.

    The buffer will be freed when the last reference to it is destroyed.

    Example:
    ```mlir
      %ch : !mef.chain
      %ctx : !mgp.context
      %size : index
      // Allocates %size bytes using the CUDA runtime from slot 5, which
      // should correspond to the CUDA GPU with virtual device id 3.
      %buf = mgp.buffer.alloc %ch, %size : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
      %buf : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    Index:$runtimeSize,
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$deviceContext,
    DefaultValuedAttr<UI64Attr, "kUnknownSize">:$rawAlign,
    MGP_OptDeviceRefAttr:$device
  );
  let results = (outs MGP_DeviceBufferType:$outBuffer);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $inChain  `,` $runtimeSize `,` $deviceContext
    ( `,` `align` $rawAlign^ )? attr-dict
    `:` custom<BufferTypeToDevice>(
          type($outBuffer), $device, type($inChain)) `,` qualified(type($deviceContext))
  }];
  let hasVerifier = 1;

  let extraClassDefinition = [{
    SmallVector<mlir::Attribute> BufferAllocOp::getIgnorableAttributes() {
      return {getRawAlignAttr(), getDeviceAttr()};
    }
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferCacheOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def BufferCacheOp : MGP_Op<"buffer.cache"> {
  let summary = "Moves an `!mgp.buffer` into a dedicated state slot.";
  let description = [{
    Stores the given `!mgp.buffer` into the state slot at the given index.
    It may be later retrieved by `mgp.buffer.get_cached`. Depending on the
    buffer's device, any computation associated with the buffer may need to be
    'finished' before the store is executed.

    If the buffer is immutable, or this op holds the only reference to the
    buffer, then it will be moved into the cache. Otherwise a deep copy of
    the buffer will be taken.

    Note this op accepts and returns `!mef.chain`s since the buffer cache is
    held on the host.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    %ctx : !mgp.context
    %buf : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
    %ch0 : !mef.chain
    // Cache the given buffer in slot index 42.
    %ch1 = mgp.buffer.cache %ch0, %ctx[5, 42], %buf
             : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
    %ch1 : !mef.chain
    ```
  }];

  // CAUTION: The attribute arguments must be in alphabetical order by their
  // names.
  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_ContextType:$theContext,
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$buffer,
    UI64Attr:$bBufferSlot
  );
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $inChain `,` $theContext `[` $bBufferSlot `]` `,`
    $buffer attr-dict `:` functional-type(operands, results)
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferFreeOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def BufferFreeOp : MGP_Op<"buffer.free"> {
  let summary = "No-op used to indicate when a buffer is freed.";
  let description = [{
    Has no primitive backing it; it only makes buffer lifetimes explicit, since
    the runtime refcounts buffers.

    Example:
    ```mlir
      %ctx : !mgp.context
      %ch1 : !mef.chain
      %buf0 : !mgp.buffer
      %ch2 = mgp.buffer.free %ch1, %buf0 : !mgp.buffer
    ```
  }];

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $inChain `,` $buffer attr-dict
    `:` custom<BufferTypeToChain>(type($buffer), type($inChain))
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$buffer
  );
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferHostToDeviceOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def BufferHostToDeviceOp : MGP_DeviceOp<"buffer.host_to_device", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_InOutSemanticsOpInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_LiftableChainCreateOpInterface>,
]> {
  let summary = "Copies a host buffer into a non-host buffer.";
  let description = [{
    Copies (typically asynchronously) the contents of an `!mgp.buffer` on the
    host device to an `!mgp.buffer` on a non-host device. The two buffers must
    agree on their runtime size.

    The output chain is ready when the copy has been scheduled, but not
    necessarily when it has completed on the device.

    Example:
    ```mlir
      %ch0 : !mef.chain
      %ctx : !mgp.context
      %host_buf : !mgp.buffer
      %other_buf : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
      %ch1 = mgp.buffer.host_to_device %ch0, %host_buf, %other_buf
               : !mgp.buffer -> !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
      %ch1 : !mef.chain
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$hostBuffer,
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$otherBuffer,
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$deviceContext,
    MGP_OptDeviceRefAttr:$hostDevice,
    MGP_OptDeviceRefAttr:$otherDevice
  );
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $inChain `,` $hostBuffer `,` $otherBuffer `,` $deviceContext attr-dict
    `:` custom<SrcDstBufferTypesToDevices>(
          type($hostBuffer), type($otherBuffer),
          $hostDevice, $otherDevice, type($inChain)) `,` qualified(type($deviceContext))
  }];
  let hasVerifier = 1;

  let extraClassDefinition = [{

    M::DeviceRefAttr BufferHostToDeviceOp::getDevice() { return getOtherDevice(); }
}];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferMemsetOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def BufferMemsetOp : MGP_DeviceOp<"buffer.memset", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_InOutSemanticsOpInterface>,
]> {
  let summary = "Fills every element of a device buffer with a scalar value.";
  let description = [{
    Sets all `elemSize`-byte elements of `buffer` to the scalar whose
    little-endian bit pattern is the low `elemSize` bytes of `valueBits`. This is
    used to initialize a persistent buffer once during the model's `init` phase.

    The value is carried as a raw bit pattern (rather than a typed attribute) so
    a single primitive can memset any element type: the graph compiler computes
    the pattern from the originating scalar and the runtime replays it with the
    device's memset.

    Example:
    ```mlir
      %ch1 = mgp.buffer.memset(%ch0, %buf, %ctx) elemSize = 4, valueBits = 0
               : (!mef.chain, !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>, !mgp.device_context<<"gpu", 3>>) -> !mef.chain
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$buffer,
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$deviceContext,
    UI64Attr:$valueBits,
    UI64Attr:$elemSize
  );
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` operands `)` `elemSize` `=` $elemSize `,` `valueBits` `=` $valueBits
        attr-dict `:` functional-type(operands, results)
  }];
  let hasVerifier = 1;

  let extraClassDefinition = [{
    M::DeviceRefAttr BufferMemsetOp::getDevice() {
      return getBuffer().getType().getDevice();
    }
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferDeviceToHostOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def BufferDeviceToHostOp : MGP_DeviceOp<"buffer.device_to_host", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_InOutSemanticsOpInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_LiftableChainCreateOpInterface>,
]> {
  let summary = "Copies a non-host buffer into a host buffer.";
  let description = [{
    Copies (typically asynchronously) the contents of an `!mgp.buffer` on a
    non-host device to an `!mgp.buffer` on the host device. The two buffers
    must agree on their runtime size.

    The output chain is ready when the copy has been scheduled, but not
    necessarily when it has completed. The device must be synchronized with
    `mgp.sync` before the host buffer can be read.

    Example:
    ```mlir
      %ch0 : !mef.chain
      %ctx : !mgp.context
      %other_buf : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
      %host_buf : !mgp.buffer
      %ch1 = mgp.buffer.device_to_host %ch0, %other_buf, %host_buf
               : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>> -> !mgp.buffer
      %ch1 : !mef.chain
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$otherBuffer,
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$hostBuffer,
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$deviceContext,
    MGP_OptDeviceRefAttr:$otherDevice,
    MGP_OptDeviceRefAttr:$hostDevice
  );
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $inChain  `,` $otherBuffer `,` $hostBuffer `,` $deviceContext attr-dict
    `:` custom<SrcDstBufferTypesToDevices>(
          type($otherBuffer), type($hostBuffer),
          $otherDevice, $hostDevice, type($inChain)) `,` qualified(type($deviceContext))
  }];
  let hasVerifier = 1;

  let extraClassDefinition = [{

    M::DeviceRefAttr BufferDeviceToHostOp::getDevice() { return getOtherDevice(); }
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferDeviceToDeviceOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def BufferDeviceToDeviceOp : MGP_DeviceOp<"buffer.device_to_device", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_InOutSemanticsOpInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_LiftableChainCreateOpInterface>,
]> {
  let summary = "Copies a non-host buffer into another non-host buffer.";
  let description = [{
    Copies (typically asynchronously) the contents of one `!mgp.buffer` into
    another `!mgp.buffer`. The two buffers must have the same device label,
    but may be on distinct virtual devices.

    The output chain is ready when the copy has been scheduled, but not
    necessarily when it has completed on the device.

    Example:
    ```mlir
      %ch0 : !mef.chain
      %ctx : !mgp.context
      %src_buf : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
      %dst_buf : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 1>>
      %ch1 = mgp.buffer.device_to_device %ch0, %ctx[5, 3], %src_buf, %dst_buf
               : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>> -> !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 1>>
      %ch1 : !mef.chain
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$srcBuffer,
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$dstBuffer,
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$srcDeviceContext,
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$dstDeviceContext,
    M_DeviceRefAttr:$srcDevice,
    M_DeviceRefAttr:$dstDevice
  );
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $inChain  `,` $srcBuffer `,` $srcDeviceContext`,` $dstBuffer `,` $dstDeviceContext attr-dict
    `:` custom<SrcDstBufferTypesToDevices>(
          type($srcBuffer), type($dstBuffer),
          $srcDevice, $dstDevice, type($inChain)) `,` qualified(type($srcDeviceContext))`,` qualified(type($dstDeviceContext))
  }];
  let hasVerifier = 1;

  let extraClassDefinition = [{

    M::DeviceRefAttr BufferDeviceToDeviceOp::getDevice() { return getDstDevice(); }
    }];

}


//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferConcatOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def BufferConcatOp : MGP_DeviceOp<"buffer.concat", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_InOutSemanticsOpInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_LiftableChainCreateOpInterface>,
]> {
  let summary = "Concatenates a sequence of input buffers into an output "
                "buffer.";
  let description = [{
    With a single input this is a buffer copy. Statically known sizes are
    checked for consistency at compile time; inconsistent runtime sizes return
    a runtime error.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    %in_ch : !mef.chain
    %out_buf : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
    %in0_buf : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
    %in1_buf : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
    %in2_buf : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
    %out_ch = mgp.buffer.concat %in_ch, %out_buf, %in0_buf, %in1_buf, %in2_buf
              : (!mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>,
                 !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>,
                 !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>) -> !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
    %out_ch : !mef.chain
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$outBuffer,
    Variadic<MGP_DeviceBufferType>:$inBuffers,
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$ctx,
    MGP_OptDeviceRefAttr:$bDevice  // 1
  );
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` operands `)` (`device` $bDevice^)? attr-dict `:`
        functional-type(operands, results)
  }];
  let hasVerifier = 1;

  let extraClassDefinition = [{

    M::DeviceRefAttr BufferConcatOp::getDevice() { return getBDevice(); }
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferPlanOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
def BufferPlanOp : MGP_Op<"buffer.plan", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface>,
  InferTypeOpAdaptor,
  Pure,
]> {
  let summary = "Runtime memory planning for buffers";
  let description = [{
    Given the size and sharing information for a list of allocations, returns
    the high watermark size and offsets for each allocation.

    canShare is a flat NxN matrix (row-major) where canShare[i*N+j]=1 iff
    allocations i and j can share the same memory slot (i.e. their lifetimes
    do not overlap). The matrix is symmetric with a zero diagonal.
    N = len(staticSizes) + len(runtimeSizes).
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    Variadic<Index>:$runtimeSizes,
    UI64ArrayElementsAttr:$alignments,
    UI8ArrayElementsAttr:$canShare,
    OptionalAttr<SI64ArrayElementsAttr>:$staticSizes
  );

  let results = (outs
    Index:$highWatermark,
    Variadic<Index>:$offsets
  );

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` $runtimeSizes `)`
      `<` `alignments` `=` qualified($alignments) `,`
      `canShare` `=` qualified($canShare)
      (`,` `staticSizes` `=` qualified($staticSizes)^)? `>`
      attr-dict `:` functional-type($runtimeSizes, results)
  }];

  let hasVerifier = 1;
  let hasCanonicalizer = 1;
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferSliceOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def BufferSliceOp : MGP_Op<"buffer.slice", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<GRTExtendsLifetimeInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<GRTMayAliasInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_LiftableBufferCreateOpInterface>,
  InferTypeOpAdaptor,
  Pure,
]> {
  let summary = "Borrows a slice of parent buffer on device with dynamically "
                "known offset and size.";
  let description = [{
    Returns a buffer borrowing the `size`-byte section of the input buffer at
    `offset`. No data is copied.

    The device context must be on the same device as the input buffer; backends
    whose runtime only accepts registered pointers register the slice through it.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    %ch:  !mef.chain
    %ctx : !mgp.device_context<<"cpu", 0>>
    %in_buf : !mgp.buffer
    %offset : index
    %size : index
    %out_buf =
        mgp.buffer.slice %in_buf, %offset, %size, %ctx
          : !mgp.buffer, !mgp.device_context<<"cpu", 0>>
    %out_buf : !mgp.buffer
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$inBuffer,
    Index:$offset,
    Index:$size,
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$deviceContext
  );

  let results = (outs MGP_DeviceBufferType:$outBuffer);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $inBuffer `,` $offset `,` $size `,` $deviceContext attr-dict `:`
      type($inBuffer) `,` qualified(type($deviceContext))
  }];

  let hasVerifier = 1;
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferBulkSliceOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def BufferBulkSliceOp : MGP_Op<"buffer.bulk_slice", [
  AttrSizedOperandSegments,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<GRTExtendsLifetimeInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<GRTMayAliasInterface>,
  InferTypeOpAdaptor,
  Pure,
]> {
  let summary = "Bulk slice of a buffer pool into N sub-buffers.";
  let description = [{
    Given a pre-allocated pool buffer and N (offset, size) pairs, produces N
    sub-buffers each borrowing a non-overlapping slice of the pool.
    Semantically equivalent to N individual `mgp.buffer.slice` ops, but
    represented as a single op to avoid stressing sequence fusion with a large
    fan-out of duplicatable slice ops.

    The device context must be on the same device as the base buffer; backends
    whose runtime only accepts registered pointers (e.g. Trainium) register each
    slice through it.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    %base : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 0>>
    %ctx : !mgp.device_context<<"gpu", 0>>
    %off0, %off1 : index
    %sz0, %sz1 : index
    %slice0, %slice1 =
        mgp.buffer.bulk_slice %base, %ctx offsets(%off0, %off1) sizes(%sz0, %sz1)
          : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 0>>, !mgp.device_context<<"gpu", 0>>
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$baseBuffer,
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$deviceContext,
    Variadic<Index>:$offsets,
    Variadic<Index>:$sizes
  );

  let results = (outs Variadic<MGP_DeviceBufferType>:$outBuffers);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $baseBuffer `,` $deviceContext `offsets` `(` $offsets `)`
      `sizes` `(` $sizes `)` attr-dict
      `:` type($baseBuffer) `,` qualified(type($deviceContext))
  }];

  let hasVerifier = 1;
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferToIndexOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def BufferToIndexOp : MGP_Op<"buffer.to_index", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<InferTypeOpInterface>,
  Pure,
]> {
  let summary = "Returns contents of the buffer to an `index`";
  let description = [{
    Returns contents of a 4- or 8-byte buffer as a 64-bit `index`.

    Sign extension is performed when upcasting from a 32-bit integer.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    %0 = mgp.buffer.to_index %ch0, %buf : !mgp.buffer
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$inBuffer
  );

  let results = (outs Index:$out);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
     $inChain `,` $inBuffer attr-dict `:` type($inBuffer)
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferToBoolOp

def BufferToBoolOp : MGP_DeviceOp<"buffer.to_bool", [

  let summary = "Returns contents of a 1-byte buffer as an i1.";

  }];

  let arguments = (ins

      `:` custom<BufferTypeToDevice>(type($buffer), $device, type($inChain))
  }];

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// BufferSetWithIndexOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def BufferSetWithIndexOp : MGP_DeviceOp<"buffer.set_with_index", [
  // TODO(#37615): Declare MGP_LiftableChainCreateOpInterface.
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_InOutSemanticsOpInterface>,
]> {
  let summary = "Set a buffer with the values from index inputs.";
  let description = [{
    The runtime index values will be sign extended or truncated based on the
    given buffer's size. Therefore only buffer sizes of 4 and 8 times the number
    of index inputs are supported by the primitive.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    %ctx : !mgp.context
    %buf0 : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
    %idx0 : index
    %ch0 = mgp.buffer.set_with_index %buf0, %idx0 : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
    %ch0 : !mef.chain

    %idx1 : index
    %idx2 : index
    %buf1 : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
    %ch1 = mgp.buffer.set_with_index %buf1, %idx0, %idx1, %idx2 : !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
    %ch1 : !mef.chain
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$buffer,
    Variadic<Index>:$values,
    MGP_OptDeviceRefAttr:$device
  );
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);
  let assemblyFormat = [{$buffer ( `,` $values^ )? attr-dict
    `:` custom<BufferTypeToDevice>(type($buffer), $device)
  }];
  let hasVerifier = 1;
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DebugTensorPrintOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def DebugTensorPrintOp : MGP_Op<"debug.tensor.print", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_SelectiveLowerAttrOpInterface, [
    "getLiftableAttributes"
  ]>,
]> {
  let summary = "Prints a debug representation of an tensor. For debugging "
                "and testing only.";
  let description = [{
    The tensor is given as an `!mgp.buffer` and `!mgp.tensor_spec`. If a label
    is supplied the contents are printed with that label, otherwise just the
    metadata. Only CPU buffers can be printed with contents; others may need an
    explicit device-to-host copy.

    Note this op accepts and returns `!mef.chain`s since printing is managed
    by the host.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    %ch0: !mef.chain
    %ctx: !mgp.context
    %buf: !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
    %spec: !mgp.tensor_spec<8x64xf32>
    %ch1 = mgp.debug.tensor.print %ch0, %ctx[5], %buf, %spec, "label"
           : !mgp.tensor<8x64xf32, <"gpu", 3>>
    %ch1: !mef.chain
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$buffer,
    MGP_TensorSpecType:$spec,
    DefaultValuedAttr<StrAttr, "\"\"">:$label
  );
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);

  let extraClassDefinition = [{
    SmallVector<Attribute> DebugTensorPrintOp::getLiftableAttributes() {
      return {getLabelAttr()};
    }
  }];

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $inChain `,` $buffer `,` $spec
    ( `,` $label^ )? attr-dict `:` functional-type(operands, results)
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// SyncOp

def MGP_SyncOp : MGP_DeviceOp<"sync", [

  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_SelectiveLowerAttrOpInterface, ["getIgnorableAttributes"]>,
  Pure,

  let summary = "Schedules a device specific sync";
  let description = [{
    Returns a ready chain once the device has synchronized. In
    cpu this is a nop as the sync happens with the chain, on
    gpu this records a gpu event.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_ContextType:$theContext,
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$deviceContext,
    MGP_OptDeviceRefAttr:$bDevice  // 1
  );
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` operands `)` (`device` $bDevice^)? attr-dict `:`
        functional-type(operands, results)
  }];

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceWaitOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_DeviceWaitOp : MGP_DeviceOp<"device_wait", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  Pure,
]> {
  let summary = "Enqueues a one-directional cross-stream wait";
  let description = [{
    Makes the waiting device context's stream wait for the work already
    enqueued on the signaling device context's stream. It records an event on
    the signaling stream and enqueues a wait for that event on the waiting
    stream.

    Unlike `mgp.sync`, this does not block the host; it only enqueues a
    cross-stream dependency. It is used to make the synchronization required by
    cross-device buffer transfers explicit in the graph instead of hidden
    inside the driver's device-to-device copy implementation.

    The `bDevice` attribute is the waiting device (the device whose stream
    receives the wait). It must be an accelerator for the op to be meaningful
    and is used for the op's device dispatch.

    The `isSideStreamJoin` attribute marks the wait that joins a side stream
    back into its base stream. MOGGToMGP moves such a wait to the first
    consumer of the side stream's results, and LowerPrimitives keeps it out of
    sequence fusion.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    ChainType:$inChain,
    MGP_ContextType:$theContext,
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$waitingDeviceContext,
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$signalingDeviceContext,
    M_DeviceRefAttr:$bDevice,
    UnitAttr:$isSideStreamJoin
  );
  let results = (outs ChainType:$outChain);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` operands `)` `device` $bDevice (`isSideStreamJoin` $isSideStreamJoin^)?
        attr-dict `:` functional-type(operands, results)
  }];

  let extraClassDefinition = [{
    M::DeviceRefAttr DeviceWaitOp::getDevice() { return getBDevice(); }
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceContextSelectStreamOp
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_DeviceContextSelectStreamOp : MGP_Op<"device_context.select_stream", [
  AllTypesMatch<["deviceContext", "view"]>,
  Pure,
]> {
  let summary = "Returns a device-context view bound to a given stream.";
  let description = [{
    Returns a "retain-all" view of the input device context whose current
    stream is `streamId`. The view shares the input context's full stream set,
    driver context, and device memory pool; only the current-stream selector
    differs.

    It binds a stream-tagged subgraph call to a side stream without threading
    per-stream device contexts through the model: the base device context is
    already an implicit model argument, so the view is derived at the call
    site. Nested selections compose since the view keeps the full stream set.

    Backends without a multi-stream model return a view equivalent to the input
    context, so all work runs on its single stream.

    It is executed directly by the MGP runtime (a primitive registered in
    `registerMGPPrimitives`, like `mgp.runtime.create`): it implements no
    `EmitsMojoInterface`, so `mgp-lower-primitives` leaves it intact and the
    executor dispatches it by name to its C++ primitive.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    MGP_DeviceContextType:$deviceContext,
    UI64Attr:$streamId
  );
  let results = (outs MGP_DeviceContextType:$view);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `[` $streamId `]` $deviceContext attr-dict `:`
        qualified(type($deviceContext))
  }];
}

#endif  // GENERICML_MGPDIALECT_MGPOPS_TD

#ifndef GENERICML_MGPDIALECT_MGPTYPES_TD
#define GENERICML_MGPDIALECT_MGPTYPES_TD

include "GraphCompiler/MGPDialect/Dialect/MGPDialect.td"
include "GraphCompiler/MGPDialect/Dialect/MGPTypeInterfaces.td"
include "MLRT/GraphRT/MEFDialect/MEFTypeInterfaces.td"
include "mlir/IR/AttrTypeBase.td"
include "mlir/IR/BuiltinTypeInterfaces.td"
include "Support/MDialect/MAttrs.td"

class MGP_Type<string name, string typeMnemonic, list<Trait> traits = []>
    : TypeDef<MGPDialect, name, traits> {
  let mnemonic = typeMnemonic;
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// ContextType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_ContextType : MGP_Type<"Context", "context",
  [DeclareTypeInterfaceMethods<MEF_AnyTypeInterface>]> {
  let summary = "Type of execution contexts holding a number of state slots.";
  let description = [{
    Contexts may be created by the 'init' entry point of a model, then reused
    by each call to the model's 'execute' entry point.

    Contexts may contain any number of 'state slots'. A state slot holds
    arbitrary data needed by operations or entire framework runtimes, such as
    attributes, scratch space, pre-computed data or cached buffers. Each op may
    declare its own state slot structure, and each call to that op in the graph
    (an 'operation') may have its own instance of that structure.

    An operator such as 'lib.foo' is generally two primitives: 'libp.foo.setup',
    invoked in 'init' to allocate and initialize a state slot, and 'libp.foo',
    which accesses that slot during 'execute'.

    Contexts are represented by `M::MGP::Context` in the Modular runtime.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    !mgp.context
    ```
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DTypeType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_DTypeType : MGP_Type<"DType", "dtype"> {
  let summary = "Runtime representation of the element type of a CPU tensor.";
  let description = [{
    A compact runtime encoding of an element type, implemented by M::DType.
    Only intended for int and float types common across modern CPUs.

    Examples:
    ```mlir
    !mgp.dtype   // A uint8_t encoding of an element type at runtime.
    ```
  }];

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    /// Returns the DType representing the given MLIR IntegerType, FloatType
    /// or NoneType. The NoneType is represented as unknown. Returns an error
    /// if the MLIR type has no representation as a DType.
    static ErrorOr<std::optional<DType>> fromMlirType(Type mlirType);

    /// Returns the MLIR IntegerType, FloatType or NoneType representing the
    /// given optDType. The unknown value is represented as the NoneType MLIR
    /// type. Returns an error if the DType has no representation as an MLIR
    /// type.
    static ErrorOr<Type> toMLIRType(MLIRContext *context, std::optional<DType> optDType);

    /// Returns error if the given optDType cannot be represented as an
    /// MLIR IntegerType, FloatType or NoneType. Otherwise returns success.
    static ErrorOrSuccess hasMLIRType(std::optional<DType> optDType);

    /// Returns the 'raw form' of optDType. This will be 0 if DType is unknown,
    /// otherwise the DType's value.
    static uint8_t asRawDType(std::optional<DType> optDType);

    /// Return the 'optional form' of rawDType. This will be none if the
    /// rawDType is 0, otherwise the DType with rawDType as value.
    static std::optional<DType> fromRawDType(uint8_t rawDType);
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// ListType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_List : MGP_Type<"List", "list",
  [DeclareTypeInterfaceMethods<MEF_AnyTypeInterface>]> {
  let summary = "Type of immutable list container.";
  let description = [{
    This type represents an immutable list of elements.
  }];

  let parameters = (ins "Type":$elementType);
  let assemblyFormat = "`<` $elementType `>`";
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// Opaque
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_OpaqueType : MGP_Type<"Opaque", "opaque",
  [DeclareTypeInterfaceMethods<MEF_AnyTypeInterface>]> {
  let summary = "Opaque MGP type";
  let description = [{
    Can represent anything; backed by an AnyAsyncValue.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    !mgp.opaque
    !mgp.opaque<{foo = "bar"}>
    ```
  }];

  let parameters = (ins "StringAttr": $symbol,
                        OptionalParameter<"std::optional<DictionaryAttr>">:$metadata);
  let assemblyFormat = "`<` $symbol (`,` $metadata^)? `>`";
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceContextType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_DeviceContextType : MGP_Type<"DeviceContext", "device_context",
  [DeclareTypeInterfaceMethods<MEF_AnyTypeInterface>]> {
  let summary = "MGP representation of the driver DeviceContext";
  let description = [{
    Essentially opaque to MGP, but represented directly so it is simpler to
    introspect.

    Examples:
    ```mlir
    // A device context for CUDA gpu 3.
    !mgp.device_context<<"gpu", 3>>
    ```
  }];

  let parameters = (ins M_DeviceRefAttr:$device);
  let assemblyFormat = "`<` $device `>`";
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceGraphType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_DeviceGraphType : MGP_Type<"DeviceGraph", "device_graph",
  [DeclareTypeInterfaceMethods<MEF_AnyTypeInterface>]> {
  let summary = "Type of a constructed device graph.";
  let description = [{
    Represents a constructed device-side graph (e.g. a CUDA graph) that can be
    replayed via `mgp.device_graph.execute`.

    The `FunctionType` signature's inputs are buffers the caller copies into
    the graph's frozen-input addresses at replay; results are buffers the graph
    writes at replay. Both are operands of `mgp.device_graph.execute`; the
    type-level split lets the synthesis pass and verifiers tell read-only from
    written operands without inspecting the build body. The target device is
    the device of the signature's `!mgp.buffer` types.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    !mgp.device_graph<
        (!mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 0>>, !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 0>>) ->
        (!mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 0>>)>
    ```
  }];

  let parameters = (ins "FunctionType":$signature);
  let assemblyFormat = "`<` $signature `>`";

  let builders = [
    TypeBuilderWithInferredContext<(ins "mlir::FunctionType":$signature)>,
    TypeBuilder<(ins "mlir::TypeRange":$inputs, "mlir::TypeRange":$results)>,
    TypeBuilder<(ins "mlir::ValueRange":$inputs, "mlir::ValueRange":$results)>,
  ];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceGraphBuilderType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_DeviceGraphBuilderType : MGP_Type<"DeviceGraphBuilder",
  "device_graph.builder",
  [DeclareTypeInterfaceMethods<MEF_AnyTypeInterface>]> {
  let summary = "Builder that records nodes into a device graph under construction.";
  let description = [{
    An opaque handle to a device-graph builder. Created in the build body of
    `mgp.device_graph.create` (from the body's `!mgp.device_context`) and
    threaded as the launch argument of `mogg.call.build_graph`, in place of the
    `!mogg.context` that `mogg.call.execute` would take. Each kernel's
    `build_graph` Mojo method records a node against the builder rather than
    dispatching immediately; once every node is recorded the builder is
    instantiated into an `!mgp.device_graph`.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    !mgp.device_graph.builder
    ```
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceGraphNodeType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_DeviceGraphNodeType : MGP_Type<"DeviceGraphNode", "device_graph.node",
  [DeclareTypeInterfaceMethods<MEF_AnyTypeInterface>]> {
  let summary = "Opaque handle to a node recorded into a device graph.";
  let description = [{
    An opaque handle to a single node recorded into a device graph via a
    kernel's `build_graph` method. Produced by `mogg.call.build_graph` and
    propagated out of the recording stub. The handle carries no structure yet;
    it exists so that future cross-stub dependency tracking can name prior
    nodes (a `depends_on` operand list) without inspecting the build body.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    !mgp.device_graph.node
    ```
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceGraphCacheType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_DeviceGraphCacheType : MGP_Type<"DeviceGraphCache",
  "device_graph.cache",
  [DeclareTypeInterfaceMethods<MEF_AnyTypeInterface>]> {
  let summary = "Opaque handle to a model's device-graph cache.";
  let description = [{
    An opaque handle to the cache of instantiated device graphs belonging to a
    model. Produced by `mgp.device_graph.cache` from the model's `!mgp.context`
    and consumed by `mgp.device_graph.create`, which reuses a cached graph
    instead of rebuilding one when the key derived from its inputs hits.

    There is one cache per model: it lives in the state context, so it is
    created on first use and outlives any single execution.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    !mgp.device_graph.cache
    ```
  }];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// TensorSpecType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_TensorSpecType : MGP_Type<"TensorSpec", "tensor_spec", [
    DeclareTypeInterfaceMethods<ShapedTypeInterface>,
]> {
  let summary = "Type of tensor specs.";
  let description = [{
    `!mgp.tensor_spec` represents the shape and dtype of a tensor.

    The rank is always static, implied by the number of dimensions (ie the
    number of `x` delimiters). Only ranks up to kMaxRank are supported
    (currently 8). A rank of zero denotes 'scalars', though in practice this
    has the same runtime representation as rank 1, dimension 1.

    Dynamic (aka unknown) dimensions and dtypes are supported:
     - Each dimension may be static (an unsigned integer literal) or dynamic
       (denoted by `?`). Symbolic dimensions are not expressible in MGP.
     - The dtype may be static (using the DType::getFromString syntax) or
       dynamic (denoted by`unk`).

    DTypes can represent most variations of MLIR IntegerType and FloatTypes.
    However:
     - Signless and non power-of-two MLIR IntegerTypes have no DType
       representation.
     - The complex and a few float DTypes have no MLIR Type representation.
     - The 'invalid' (zero) DType is never permitted.
    If a tensor spec is given a DType we also require it to be representable as
    an MLIR type.

    This type implements ShapedTypeInterface. We'll use 'dims'/'dtype' when
    referring to our internal representation, and 'shape'/'element type' when
    referring to the ShapedTypeInterface representation.

    Representations in flight:
     - For dimensions:
        - 'optional' form: std::optional<uint64_t>, where nullopt denotes
          a dynamic dimension.
        - 'signed' form: int64_t, where ShapedType::kDynamicSize denotes
          a dynamic dimension. As used by ShapedTypeInterface.
        - 'raw' form: uint64_t, where ~0 denotes a dynamic dimension. Used
          when dimensions need to be encoded into MEF ops via attributes.
     - For shapes:
        - 'optional' form: ArrayRef<std::optional<uint64_t>>.
        - 'shaped type' form: ArrayRef<int64_t>, as used by ShapedTypeInterface.
        - 'raw' form: IntArrayElementsAttr of UI64Ints.
     - For dtypes:
        - 'optional' form: std::optional<DType>, where nullopt denotes a
          dynamic dtype.
        - 'shaped type' form: An MLIR type, where NoneType denotes a dynamic
          dtype.
        - 'raw' form: uint8_t, where 0 (ie invalid) denotes a dynamic dtype.

    `!mgp.tensor_specs` are represented by `MLRT::AsyncValueRef<M::TensorSpec>`
    in the host C++ runtime. All dimensions in the runtime value should 'refine'
    the corresponding compile time spec, ie runtime dims must equal statically
    known compile-time dims.

    Examples:
    ```mlir
    // Fully statically known spec.
    !mgp.tensor_spec<4x16xf32>
    // Spec with one dynamic dimension and dynamic dtype.
    !mgp.tensor_spec<?x3xunk>
    ```
  }];

  // NOTE: To support the ShapedTypeInterface::getShape() method we maintain
  // 'optional' (dimsOrEmpty) and 'shaped type' (shapeOrEmpty) forms.
  // See the builders for the smart constructors.
  let parameters = (ins
    ArrayRefParameter<"std::optional<uint64_t>">:$dimsOrEmpty,
    "std::optional<DType>":$optDType,
    ArrayRefParameter<"int64_t">:$shapeOrEmpty
  );

  let assemblyFormat = "`<` custom<DimsAndDType>($dimsOrEmpty, $optDType, $shapeOrEmpty) `>`";
  let genVerifyDecl = 1;

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    /// For the ShapedTypeInterface we implement:
    ///   bool hasRank(); // always true.
    ///   ShapedType cloneWith(std::optional<ArrayRef<int64_t>> shape,
    ///                        Type elementType);
    ///   Type getElementType();
    ///   ArrayRef<int64_t> getShape();

    /// Returns the dimensions of this tensor spec.
    llvm::ArrayRef<std::optional<uint64_t>> getDims() const;

    /// Returns the rank of this tensor spec.
    size_t getRank() const;

    /// Returns the number of unknown, aka 'dynamic' dimensions in
    /// this tensor spec.
    size_t getNumDynamicDims() const;

    /// Return the dimension at index i in this spec, or nullopt if the
    /// dimension is dynamic.
    std::optional<uint64_t> operator[](size_t i) const;

    /// Returns the number of elements in a tensor of this spec, or
    /// nullopt if the tensor shape is not fully static (ie at least one
    /// dynamic dimension).
    std::optional<uint64_t> getNumElements() const;

    /// Returns the size of the buffer needed to represent a tensor
    /// of this spec, or nullopt if the tensor spec is not fully static
    /// (ie at least one dynamic dimension, or dynamic dtype).
    std::optional<uint64_t> getSizeInBytes() const;

    /// Returns the dimensions of this tensor spec in 'raw form'.
    /// Each element of the result will be an UI64Int, with ~0 denoting
    /// an unknown dimension.
    IntArrayElementsAttr getRawDims() const;

    /// Returns the dtype of this tensor spec in 'raw form'.
    /// The result will be a UI8Int using the DType::value encoding,
    /// with 0 denoting the unknown dtype.
    mlir::IntegerAttr getRawDType() const;
  }];

  let builders = [
    /// Constructs a tensor spec from its components in 'optional' form.
    TypeBuilder<(ins "llvm::ArrayRef<std::optional<uint64_t>>":$dims,
                     "std::optional<DType>":$optDType)>,

    /// Constructs a tensor spec from its components in 'shaped type' form.
    TypeBuilderWithInferredContext<(ins "llvm::ArrayRef<int64_t>":$shape,
                                        "mlir::Type":$elementType)>,

    /// Construct a tensor spec from its components in 'raw form',
    /// using underlying integer values.
    TypeBuilder<(ins "llvm::ArrayRef<uint64_t>":$rawDims, "uint8_t":$rawDType)>,

    /// Construct a tensor spec from its components in 'raw form', using
    /// actual attributes. As a convenience, the null dtype attribute is taken
    /// to denote the unknown element type.
    TypeBuilderWithInferredContext<(ins "IntArrayElementsAttr":$rawDims,
                                        "mlir::IntegerAttr":$rawDTypeOrNull)>,
  ];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
//
// Device-generic types in the MGP dialect. All of these types accept an
// #M.device_ref attribute indicating the specific type and 'virtual' device
// id the type should apply to.
//
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

class MGP_DeviceType<string name, string mnemonic, list<Trait> traits = []> :
    MGP_Type<
      name,
      mnemonic,
      [DeclareTypeInterfaceMethods<MGP_HasDeviceTypeInterface>] # traits
    >;

def MGP_OptDeviceRefParam :
  DefaultValuedParameter<"M::DeviceRefAttr",
                         "M::DeviceRefAttr::getDefault($_ctxt)">;

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceBufferType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_DeviceBufferType : MGP_DeviceType<"DeviceBuffer", "buffer", [
    DeclareTypeInterfaceMethods<ShapedTypeInterface>,
]> {
  let summary = "Byte array buffers.";
  let description = [{
    `!mgp.buffer`s are mutable byte arrays which reside on the device given by
    the `#M.device_ref` attribute.

    Nothing is implied about the internal structure of the bytes, such as rank,
    dimensions, underlying element type, padding, or element endianness. The
    compiler is responsible for ensuring the producers and consumers of buffers
    agree on their interpretation of the buffer for the intended device.

    Generally `!mgp.buffer`s are the lowest-common denominator representation
    of tensor data across kernel implementations. Buffers may be wrapped by
    various tensor types, including `!mgp.tensor`, or used directly.

    This type implements `ShapedTypeInterface` as a rank-1 tensor over
    `uint8_t`. This in turn supports the `ElementsAttrInterface` on buffer
    attributes.

    Alignment constraints are specified at buffer creation or in the attribute
    backing a constant buffer, not in the buffer type.

    Since buffers are mutable, any op reading a buffer must accept a
    `!mef.chain`, and any op writing one must return a `!mef.chain`, so the
    compiler can sequence writes and reads.

    `!mgp.buffer`s are represented by (subclasses of)
    `MLRT::AsyncValueRef<BufferRef>` in the host C++ runtime. Some devices,
    such as CUDA, may need to include additional data to control device-side
    synchronization.

    Examples:
    ```mlir
    // A buffer on the CUDA GPU with virtual device id 3.
    !mgp.buffer<<"gpu", 3>>
    // A buffer on the CPU with virtual device id 0.
    !mgp.buffer<<"cpu", 0>>
    // Abbreviation for the above.
    !mgp.buffer
    ```
  }];

  let parameters = (ins MGP_OptDeviceRefParam:$device);
  let assemblyFormat = "(`<` $device^ `>`)?";
  let genVerifyDecl = 1;

  let builders = [
    /// Constructs a buffer type from the given device.
    TypeBuilderWithInferredContext<(ins "M::DeviceRefAttr":$device)>,

    /// Constructs a buffer type which matches the device and any other properties
    /// of the given tensor type.
    TypeBuilderWithInferredContext<(ins "M::MGP::DeviceTensorType":$tensorType)>,
  ];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// DeviceTensorType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_DeviceTensorType : MGP_DeviceType<"DeviceTensor", "tensor", [
    DeclareTypeInterfaceMethods<ShapedTypeInterface>,
]> {
  let summary = "Type of tensors respecting a tensor spec.";
  let description = [{
    `!mgp.tensor`s are tensors consisting of a buffer and a tensor spec, where
    the buffer resides on the device given by the `#M.device_ref` attribute.
    The elements in the buffer are generally in dense row-major order
    according to the runtime tensor spec, with endianness according to the
    device's architecture.

    Tensors are immutable unless marked `mut`. When an immutable tensor is
    created from a buffer, the buffer must be copied if it could still be
    written. When a buffer is extracted from an immutable tensor, the buffer
    must be copied if the tensor could still be read.

    The `mut` marker is the lowered form of `!mo.buffer`: a tensor the model
    writes in place through explicitly chained ops (a KV cache, for example).

    The `stable` marker indicates that the tensor's underlying address is
    stable across dispatches and may participate in cross-device coordination
    mechanisms such as `!mgp.stable_addr` slots. A tensor may be both `mut` and
    `stable`.

    `!mgp.tensor`s are represented by (subclasses of)
    `MLRT::AsyncValueRef<Tensor>` in the host C++ runtime, and the underlying
    buffer may also be passed as a raw `void*`. Some devices, such as CUDA, may
    need additional data to control device-side synchronization.

    Examples:
    ```mlir
    // Statically-shaped tensor on the CUDA GPU with virtual device id 3.
    !mgp.tensor<4x16xf32, <"gpu", 3>>
    // Dynamically-shaped tensor on the CPU with virtual device id 0.
    !mgp.tensor<?x?xf32, <"cpu", 0>>
    // Abbreviation for the above.
    !mgp.tensor<?x?xf32>
    // A mutable tensor (lowered from !mo.buffer) on GPU 0.
    !mgp.tensor<464x4800xf16, <"gpu", 0>, mut>
    // A stable tensor on GPU 0.
    !mgp.tensor<4x16xf32, <"gpu", 0>, stable>
    // A mutable, stable tensor on GPU 0.
    !mgp.tensor<4x16xf32, <"gpu", 0>, mut, stable>
    ```
  }];

  let parameters = (ins
    MGP_OptDeviceRefParam:$device,
    "M::MGP::TensorSpecType":$tensorSpec,
    DefaultValuedParameter<"bool", "false">:$mut,
    DefaultValuedParameter<"bool", "false">:$stable
  );

  // The device, mut, and stable tail share one custom directive: the optional
  // groups would otherwise start with `,`, which the generated parser cannot
  // disambiguate.
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `<` custom<TensorSpec>($tensorSpec) `` custom<DeviceTensorTail>($device, $mut, $stable) `>`
  }];

  let builders = [
    /// Constructs an immutable, non-stable tensor type from the given device
    /// and tensor spec.
    TypeBuilderWithInferredContext<(ins "M::DeviceRefAttr":$device,
                                        "M::MGP::TensorSpecType":$tensorSpecType)>,

    /// Constructs a tensor type from the given device, tensor spec, and
    /// mutability. The result is not stable.
    TypeBuilderWithInferredContext<(ins "M::DeviceRefAttr":$device,
                                        "M::MGP::TensorSpecType":$tensorSpecType,
                                        "bool":$mut)>,

    /// Constructs a tensor type from the given device, tensor spec,
    /// mutability, and stability.
    TypeBuilderWithInferredContext<(ins "M::DeviceRefAttr":$device,
                                        "M::MGP::TensorSpecType":$tensorSpecType,
                                        "bool":$mut,
                                        "bool":$stable)>,
  ];
}

//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//
// StableAddressType
//===----------------------------------------------------------------------===//

def MGP_StableAddressType : MGP_Type<"StableAddress", "stable_addr"> {
  let summary = "Handle to a stable address slot for cross-device coordination.";
  let description = [{
    Inside a device-graph body, `mgp.device_graph.stable.place` publishes a
    value into the slot and `mgp.device_graph.stable.get` reads it; both return
    the slot. `mgp.device_graph.stable.tensor` views the slot as the
    `!mgp.tensor<..., stable>` it holds, and a kernel handed that tensor reads
    through the slot via a `stable`-marked `!mo.tensor`.

    This type is the MGP-level handle into the low-level allocation and
    pointer-patching mechanism.

    The `elementType` parameter records the `!mgp.tensor` type held by the
    slot, so a view built over the slot knows its shape and device.
  }];
  let parameters = (ins MGP_DeviceTensorType:$elementType);
  let assemblyFormat = "`<` $elementType `>`";

  let builders = [
    /// Builds a `!mgp.stable_addr<T>` without an explicit context, reusing the
    /// context of the wrapped tensor type.
    TypeBuilderWithInferredContext<(ins "Type":$tensorType), [{
      return $_get(tensorType.getContext(),
                    llvm::cast<DeviceTensorType>(tensorType));
    }]>,
  ];
}

struct IndexLowering {
  MGP::MOOpLoweringState &opLoweringState;

  // Arithmetic helpers
  auto constant(int64_t val) -> Value {
    return opLoweringState.create<mlir::index::ConstantOp>(val);
  }

  auto mul(Value a, Value b) -> Value {
    auto indexTy = opLoweringState.builder.getIndexType();
    return opLoweringState.create<mlir::index::MulOp>(indexTy, a, b);
  }

  auto add(Value a, Value b) -> Value {
    auto indexTy = opLoweringState.builder.getIndexType();
    return opLoweringState.create<mlir::index::AddOp>(indexTy, a, b);
  }

  auto div(Value a, Value b) -> Value {
    auto indexTy = opLoweringState.builder.getIndexType();
    return opLoweringState.create<mlir::index::DivSOp>(indexTy, a, b);
  }

  // `pop.select` takes a `!kgen.scalar<bool>` condition, but `index.cmp`
  // produces an `i1`. Convert the builtin `i1` to `!kgen.scalar<bool>`.
  auto asScalarBool(Value i1Cond) -> Value {
    auto boolTy = KGEN::SIMDType::get(opLoweringState.builder.getContext(), 1,
                                      KGEN::KGENDType::kBool);
    return opLoweringState.create<KGEN::POP::CastFromBuiltinOp>(boolTy, i1Cond);
  }

  auto ifPositive(Value check, Value yes, Value no) -> Value {
    auto indexTy = opLoweringState.builder.getIndexType();
    auto cond = opLoweringState.create<mlir::index::CmpOp>(
        mlir::index::IndexCmpPredicate::SLT, check, constant(0));
    return opLoweringState.create<KGEN::POP::SelectOp>(
        indexTy, asScalarBool(cond), no, yes);
  }

  auto ifZero(Value check, Value yes, Value no) -> Value {
    auto indexTy = opLoweringState.builder.getIndexType();
    auto cond = opLoweringState.create<mlir::index::CmpOp>(
        mlir::index::IndexCmpPredicate::EQ, check, constant(0));
    return opLoweringState.create<KGEN::POP::SelectOp>(
        indexTy, asScalarBool(cond), yes, no);
  }
};

/// Lowers one mo.graph to an mgp.model with an 'init' phase, an 'execute'
/// phase, and a model descriptor.
class MOGraphLowering {
public:
  MOGraphLowering(MO::GraphOp graph, llvm::StringRef compiledFrameworkLabel,
                  size_t minimumCpuAlignment,
                  mlir::SymbolTable &moduleSymbolTable)
      : loweringState(graph, compiledFrameworkLabel, minimumCpuAlignment,
                      moduleSymbolTable) {}

  /// Lower the mo.graph to mgp.model.
  LogicalResult run();

  // Establish type builders for all the (virtual) devices needed by the model.
  LogicalResult setupTypeBuildersForAllDevices(MO::GraphOp graph);

  // Establish buffer builders for all the (virtual) devices needed by the
  // model. Each device will have its 'runtime' created in the 'init' block
  // and held in the !mgp.context.
  CompileDiagnosticOrSuccess setupBufferBuildersForAllDevices();

  LogicalResult createModelOp();

  /// Lowers a MO::ListType to a MGP::ListType.
  MGP::ListType lowerListType(MO::ListType listTy);

  /// Clones a trivial operations that does not need transformation. E.g.,
  /// `index.constant`
  LogicalResult cloneTrivialOp(Operation *trivialOp);

  /// Returns an attribute to represent elementAttr for the remainder of
  /// compilation:
  ///  - We commit to a specific byte layout, ie from here on the attribute
  ///    is considered an ArrayRef<uint8_t> with no further interpretation.
  ///  - Large attributes are outlined as dense_resources.
  ///  - The required runtime alignment is captured as an !M.aligned_bytes type.
  ///  - The runtime alignment will be at least 'minimumCpuAlignment' from
  ///    the pass options.
  ///  - If elementAttr already has an !M.aligned_bytes type annotation, that
  ///    may increase the alignment. Otherwise, if the attribute itself has some
  ///    indication of alignment (eg a dense_resource's blob's alignment) that
  ///    may increase the alignment.
  ///  - However the result's underlying data may not respect the alignment.
  ///    Instead we assume alignment is enforced on serialization to MEF.
  ///    This helps us avoid gratuitous memory copies.
  ///  - No data is copied.
  ErrorOr<ElementsAttr> lowerElementsAttr(ElementsAttr elementsAttr) {
    return loweringState.lowerElementsAttr(elementsAttr);
  }

  /// Per-op lowering overloads. Each concrete MO/MOGG/KGEN op type has a
  /// corresponding `lower()` overload; `lowerOp()` dispatches to these via
  /// TypeSwitch.
  LogicalResult lower(MO::OutputOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::YieldOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::WhileConditionOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::IndexToTensorOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::Shape::ToTensorOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::Shape::FromTensorOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::RebindOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::ConstantOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::ConstantExternalOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::ConstantScalarOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::DebugPrintOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::DebugTensorPrintOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::TransferOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::StableCreateOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::IfOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::WhileOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::GuardOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::ChainCreateOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::MutableStoreOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::MutableLoadOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::BufferCreateOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::BufferTransferOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::CallOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::ParallelOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::SequenceOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::TensorBundleOp op);
  LogicalResult lower(MO::TensorUnbundleOp op);

  /// Param ops need the enclosing region to resolve parameter expressions.
  LogicalResult lowerParam(Region *parentRegion, KGEN::ParamDeclareOp op);
  LogicalResult lowerParam(Region *parentRegion, MOSH::ParamToValueOp op);
  LogicalResult lowerParam(Region *parentRegion, MOSH::ParamFromValueOp op);

  /// Interface-based lowering for externally-defined ops.
  LogicalResult lowerInterface(MGP::LowerableToMGPInterface op);

private:
  /// Lowers a single Operation via type-based dispatch.
  LogicalResult lowerOp(Operation &op, mlir::Region *parentRegion);

  /// Lowers a Block
  LogicalResult lowerBlock(mlir::Block *block);

  MGP::MOGraphLoweringState loweringState;
};

} // namespace

static SmallVector<DeviceRefAttr> getAllDevicesUsedInGraph(MO::GraphOp graph) {
  llvm::DenseSet<DeviceRefAttr> devices;

  // The host device may not appear in the graph.
  DeviceRefAttr hostDevice = DeviceRefAttr::getDefault(graph->getContext());
  devices.insert(hostDevice);

  mlir::AttrTypeWalker walker;
  walker.addWalk([&](DeviceRefAttr attr) { devices.insert(attr); });
  graph->walk([&](Operation *op) {
    walker.walk(op->getAttrDictionary());
    for (Type type : op->getOperands().getTypes())
      walker.walk(type);
    for (Type type : op->getResultTypes())
      walker.walk(type);
    for (Region &region : op->getRegions()) {
      for (Type type : region.getArgumentTypes())
        walker.walk(type);
    }
  });

  // Host first, then the rest by string representation, for a stable order.
  SmallVector<DeviceRefAttr> sorted = llvm::to_vector(devices);
  llvm::sort(sorted.begin(), sorted.end(),
             [hostDevice](DeviceRefAttr left, DeviceRefAttr right) {
               if (left == hostDevice)
                 return true;
               if (right == hostDevice)
                 return false;
               return left.toString() < right.toString();
             });
  return sorted;
}

LogicalResult
MOGraphLowering::setupTypeBuildersForAllDevices(MO::GraphOp graph) {
  for (DeviceRefAttr device : getAllDevicesUsedInGraph(graph))
    loweringState.registerTypeBuilder(device);
  return success();
}

CompileDiagnosticOrSuccess MOGraphLowering::setupBufferBuildersForAllDevices() {
  DeviceRefAttr hostDevice =
      DeviceRefAttr::getDefault(loweringState.getModelOp()->getContext());

  auto makeBufferBuilder =
      [&](DeviceRefAttr targetDevice) -> CompileDiagnosticOrSuccess {
    MGP::MGPBufferBuilder *hostBufferBuilder;
    auto bufferBuilder = std::make_unique<MGP::MGPBufferBuilder>(targetDevice);
    if (hostDevice == targetDevice) {
      hostBufferBuilder = bufferBuilder.get();
    } else {
      hostBufferBuilder = &loweringState.getBufferBuilder(hostDevice);
    }
    auto inChain =
        cast<TypedValue<MEF::ChainType>>(loweringState.getInitChain());
    auto chain = bufferBuilder->setupForModel(
        loweringState.getModelOp(), hostBufferBuilder,
        loweringState.getInitOpBuilder(), loweringState.getGraph()->getLoc(),
        inChain);
    loweringState.setInitChain(chain);
    loweringState.registerBufferBuilder(targetDevice, std::move(bufferBuilder));
    return success();
  };

  if (auto err = makeBufferBuilder(hostDevice); err.isError())
    return err;

  for (auto device : getAllDevicesUsedInGraph(loweringState.getGraph())) {
    if (device != hostDevice) {
      if (auto err = makeBufferBuilder(device); err.isError())
        return err;
    }
  }

  return success();
}

// Create the mgp.model and the regions for the init/execute phases.
LogicalResult MOGraphLowering::createModelOp() {
  MO::GraphOp &graph = loweringState.getGraph();
  OpBuilder b(graph);

  // Establish type builders for all the devices.
  // CAUTION: Must be done before any types are lowered, eg the next
  // paragraph.
  if (failed(setupTypeBuildersForAllDevices(graph)))
    return failure();

  // Convert the tensor types for the model signature over.
  SmallVector<Type> inputTypes, outputTypes;
  if (failed(loweringState.getTypeConverter().convertTypes(
          graph.getArgumentTypes(), inputTypes))) {
    return graph.emitOpError("failed to convert mo graph input types")
           << graph.getArgumentTypes() << " is not supported";
  } else if (failed(loweringState.getTypeConverter().convertTypes(
                 graph.getResultTypes(), outputTypes))) {
    return graph.emitOpError("failed to convert mo graph output types -- ")
           << graph.getResultTypes() << " is not supported";
  }

  // Preserve the MO::GraphOp argument locations in the MGP::ModelOp 'execute'
  // block argument locations.
  SmallVector<Location> inputLocs;
  for (BlockArgument arg : graph.getBody().front().getArguments())
    inputLocs.push_back(arg.getLoc());

  // Collect additional attributes to include with the MGP::ModelOp to guide
  // the MEF executor.
  SmallVector<NamedAttribute> extraAttrs;

  ArrayAttr argNamesAttr =
      graph->getAttrOfType<ArrayAttr>(kMgpModelArgumentNames);
  ArrayAttr resultNamesAttr =
      graph->getAttrOfType<ArrayAttr>(kMgpModelResultNames);
  ASSERT_STREAM(
      (argNamesAttr == nullptr) == (resultNamesAttr == nullptr),
      << "expected either both or neither of the `argument_names` and "
         "`result_names` attributes.");
  if (argNamesAttr) {
    extraAttrs.emplace_back(b.getStringAttr(kMgpModelArgumentNames),
                            argNamesAttr);
    extraAttrs.emplace_back(b.getStringAttr(kMgpModelResultNames),
                            resultNamesAttr);
  }

  ErrorOrSuccess err(success());
  auto devices = llvm::map_to_vector(getAllDevicesUsedInGraph(graph),
                                     [&err](DeviceRefAttr attr) {
                                       auto refOr = toRuntimeDeviceRef(attr);
                                       if (refOr.isError()) {
                                         err = refOr.takeError();
                                         return DeviceRef();
                                       } else {
                                         return refOr.takeValue();
                                       }
                                     });
  if (err.isError())
    return err;

  auto ctx = graph->getContext();
  SmallDenseMap<DeviceRefAttr, IntegerAttr> deviceIndexMap;
  auto idxType = IntegerType::get(ctx, 32, IntegerType::Unsigned);
  for (const auto &[idx, deviceRef] :
       llvm::enumerate(getAllDevicesUsedInGraph(graph)))
    deviceIndexMap[deviceRef] = IntegerAttr::get(idxType, idx);
  auto populateDeviceIndicesExtraAttr = [&](const char *label,
                                            SmallVector<Type> types) {
    llvm::SmallVector<Attribute> deviceIndices;
    for (const auto &type : types) {
      if (auto hasDeviceType = dyn_cast<MGP::MGPHasDeviceTypeInterface>(type))
        deviceIndices.push_back(deviceIndexMap[hasDeviceType.getDevice()]);
    }
    if (!deviceIndices.empty()) {
      ArrayAttr deviceIndicesAttr = ArrayAttr::get(ctx, deviceIndices);
      extraAttrs.emplace_back(b.getStringAttr(label), deviceIndicesAttr);
    }
  };
  populateDeviceIndicesExtraAttr(kMgpModelArgumentDeviceIndices, inputTypes);
  populateDeviceIndicesExtraAttr(kMgpModelResultDeviceIndices, outputTypes);

  b.setInsertionPoint(graph);
  auto modelOp = MGP::ModelOp::create(
      b, graph.getLoc(),
      /*name=*/graph.getNameAttr(),
      /*frameworkName=*/loweringState.getCompiledFrameworkLabel(),
      /*devices=*/devices,
      /*inputTypes=*/inputTypes,
      /*outputTypes=*/outputTypes,
      /*inputArgLocs=*/inputLocs,
      /*isSubgraph=*/graph.getIsSubgraph(),
      /*isDeviceGraph=*/graph.getIsDeviceGraph(),
      /*extraAttrs=*/extraAttrs);

  loweringState.setModelOp(modelOp);

  // The model takes over the graph's symbol name. The cached
  // `SymbolTableAnalysis` is never invalidated by the pass manager, so update
  // it by hand; the graph stays in the IR until the end of `run()`.
  mlir::SymbolTable &moduleSymbolTable = loweringState.getModuleSymbolTable();
  moduleSymbolTable.remove(graph);
  moduleSymbolTable.insert(modelOp);

  loweringState.getInitOpBuilder().setInsertionPointToEnd(
      loweringState.getModelOp().getInitBlock());
  // Tracks the current init output chain.
  loweringState.setInitChain(GRT::ChainCreateOp::create(
      loweringState.getInitOpBuilder(), graph.getLoc()));

  // Create the !mgp.context. Its numSlots attribute will be incremented
  // as needed.
  loweringState.setInitMgpContext(MGP::ContextCreateOp::create(
      loweringState.getInitOpBuilder(), graph.getLoc(), /*numSlots=*/0));

  // Initialize the execute state.
